lessons.title: $ % ^ &: the index fingers
lessons.tip: These four symbols are on the 4, 5, 6 and 7 keys with Shift: your index fingers reach them, just as for the numbers.

tuto.intro: The symbols on the number row are typed with Shift. We start with those of the index fingers: $ and % on 4 and 5 for the left hand, ^ and & on 6 and 7 for the right hand. The exact movement for your keyboard is shown just below.

rules.d: Just like capital letters: hold Shift with the little finger of the hand that is not typing the key. Shift plus the number key gives the symbol.

rules.t: The same keys as the numbers
rules.d: You already know these keys: 4 5 6 7. Only the Shift press changes. Your index finger reaches up, types, and drops back to F or J.
On a US International keyboard, ^ ~ and ` are dead keys: type the symbol, then press the space bar so that it appears on its own.

tuto.tip: Goal: type $ % ^ & with Shift and the index fingers, without looking.

lessons.title: # and *: the middle fingers
lessons.tip: The hash is on the 3 key and the asterisk on the 8 key, with Shift: your middle fingers reach up.

tuto.intro: The middle fingers cover the hash # (3 key, left hand) and the asterisk * (8 key, right hand). The hash starts a hashtag, and the asterisk is used in sums and lists. The exact movement for your keyboard is shown just below.

rules.d: Just like capital letters: hold Shift with the little finger of the hand that is not typing the key. Shift plus the number key gives the symbol.
#news #help #music: a word preceded by # is a hashtag. Type the hash, then the word, with no space.
3*4 reads as "three times four". You also see it as a marker or a wildcard.

tuto.tip: Goal: type # and * with Shift and the middle fingers.

lessons.title: @: the at sign
lessons.tip: The at sign is on the 2 key, with Shift: your left ring finger reaches up, with right Shift.

tuto.intro: The at sign links a person's name and the domain of an email address: anna@mail.example. On QWERTY, it is on the 2 key, with Shift. The exact movement for your keyboard is shown just below.

rules.d: Just like capital letters: hold Shift with the little finger of the hand that is not typing the key. Shift plus the number key gives the symbol.

rules.t: The heart of an email address
rules.d: info@shop.example: the name, @, then the domain. No spaces are allowed in an address.
The ring finger is less agile than the index finger: reach up gently to the 2, and hold Shift with your right little finger.

tuto.tip: Goal: type @ with Shift + 2, in complete addresses.

lessons.title: _ + =: the right little finger
lessons.tip: The underscore, plus and equals signs are on the keys to the right of the 0: your right little finger reaches right to the end of the row.

tuto.intro: Right at the end of the number row, your right little finger reaches three signs: the underscore _ (Shift + hyphen), the plus + (Shift + equals) and the equals = (no Shift). The exact movement for your keyboard is shown just below.

rules.d: The keys to the right of the 0 are the furthest away: stretch only your little finger, and keep your wrist steady.
_ and + need Shift (with your left little finger); = is typed on its own. The plain hyphen seen earlier is the _ key without Shift.
my_name, file_name, a+b=c: the underscore joins words in code names, and the plus and equals signs do sums.

tuto.tip: Goal: reach _ + = with your right little finger, returning to the home row.

lessons.text: a+b=c x_y my_name file_name 2+3=5 total_score a_b+c_d 4+4=8 one_two 1+1=2 9=9 big_cat+dog=pets

lessons.title: ` and ~: the left little finger
lessons.tip: The backtick and the tilde are on the key at the top left, under Esc: your left little finger reaches it, with Shift for the tilde.

tuto.intro: Right at the top left, your left little finger reaches the key for the backtick ` and the tilde ~ (with Shift). You see them in code and in file paths: ~/documents. The exact movement for your keyboard is shown just below.

rules.t: The left little finger reaches up
rules.d: This key is to the left of the 1. Your left little finger reaches it; the tilde needs Shift with your right little finger.
On a US International keyboard, ^ ~ and ` are dead keys: type the symbol, then press the space bar so that it appears on its own.
`code` wraps a piece of code; ~/documents points to the home folder. Two signs, one single stretching movement.

tuto.tip: Goal: type ` and ~ with your left little finger, using the right movement for your keyboard.

lessons.title: Review: the number-row symbols
lessons.tip: You bring all the number-row symbols together in a text. Identify the finger and the Shift key before you go for the sign.

tuto.intro: You bring the number-row symbols together in a text: addresses, prices, sums, variable names, paths. The exact movement for your keyboard is shown just below.

rules.t: Identify the sign before typing it
rules.d: Which finger? Which hand for Shift? This reflex saves you time on every symbol.
The movement is always the same: opposite-hand Shift, the key, then release both.
A wrong symbol breaks an address or a command. Slow down on the ones that give you trouble.

tuto.tip: Goal: chain all the number-row symbols together in real text.
